books.title: The Annals
books.subtitle: The Reigns of Tiberius, Claudius, and Nero
books.author: Tacitus
books.summary: A year-by-year Roman history of the Julio-Claudian emperors from the death of Augustus to the reign of Nero, covering court politics, provincial revolts, and the fire of Rome.
books.note: Oxford World's Classics, translated by J. C. Yardley. The episode cites Annals 12.54.

books.title: An Anthropologist Among the Historians and Other Essays
books.author: Bernard S. Cohn
books.summary: A collection of essays on the methods and relationship of anthropology and history, applied chiefly to Indian society and British colonial rule.

books.title: Colonialism and Its Forms of Knowledge
books.subtitle: The British in India
books.author: Bernard S. Cohn
books.summary: Argues that British efforts to collect and codify knowledge about Indian languages, law, history, objects, and dress were themselves instruments of colonial rule.

books.title: The Great Fear
books.subtitle: The Anti-Communist Purge Under Truman and Eisenhower
books.author: David Caute
books.summary: A detailed history of the postwar campaign against suspected Communists: loyalty programs, congressional investigations, trials, and blacklists.

books.title: Hear Then the Parable
books.subtitle: A Commentary on the Parables of Jesus
books.author: Bernard Brandon Scott
books.summary: Examines each of the parables of Jesus through literary and social-historical analysis, reconstructing their earliest forms and reading them against the social world of first-century Galilee.

books.title: Jericho
books.subtitle: The Jewish Cemetery of the Second Temple Period
books.author: Rachel Hachlili and Ann E. Killebrew
books.summary: The final excavation report on the Jewish cemetery at Jericho, documenting its rock-cut tombs, coffins, ossuaries, inscriptions and burial customs of the Second Temple period.

books.title: Jerusalem in the Time of Jesus
books.subtitle: An Investigation into Economic and Social Conditions during the New Testament Period
books.author: Joachim Jeremias
books.summary: A historical reconstruction of the economic and social structure of first-century Jerusalem, examining trade, wealth and poverty, the priesthood, lay aristocracy, scribes, Pharisees, and the maintenance of racial purity.
books.note: The episode discusses this book as an example of the older reading it challenges, not as a source for its own argument.

books.title: Jesus
books.subtitle: Apocalyptic Prophet of the New Millennium
books.author: Bart D. Ehrman
books.summary: Presents Jesus as a Jewish apocalyptic preacher who expected God to intervene in history within his own generation.

books.title: Jesus
books.subtitle: A Revolutionary Biography
books.author: John Dominic Crossan
books.summary: A historical reconstruction of Jesus's life and teaching, drawing on social-scientific study of first-century Mediterranean society.

books.title: Jesus the Jew
books.subtitle: A Historian's Reading of the Gospels
books.author: Geza Vermes
books.summary: Places Jesus within the charismatic Judaism of first-century Galilee, reading the Gospels as a historian of Judaism.

books.title: Judaism
books.subtitle: Practice and Belief, 63 BCE–66 CE
books.author: E. P. Sanders
books.summary: Argues that ordinary 'common Judaism'—Temple worship, sacrifice, purity, tithes and shared theology—rather than Pharisaic or rabbinic teaching defined Jewish religious life in Palestine between 63 BCE and 66 CE.

books.title: Land and Temple
books.subtitle: Field Sacralization and the Agrarian Priesthood of Second Temple Judaism
books.author: Benjamin D. Gordon
books.summary: Examines the Judean priesthood's involvement in agriculture and the consecration of fields to the Temple, arguing that Second Temple sacred space and priestly authority extended into farmland beyond the sanctuary.

books.title: The Limits of Power
books.subtitle: The End of American Exceptionalism
books.author: Andrew J. Bacevich
books.summary: Argues that American overreach and political dysfunction have outrun the country's means, and that a more restrained foreign policy is needed.

books.title: Luke
books.subtitle: New International Biblical Commentary
books.author: Craig A. Evans
books.summary: A verse-by-verse commentary on the Gospel of Luke for general readers and students.
books.ebookNote: The ebook is the Baker Books reissue in the Understanding the Bible Commentary series.

books.title: Luke
books.subtitle: A New Paradigm
books.author: Michael D. Goulder
books.summary: Argues that Luke composed his Gospel using Mark and Matthew rather than Q or a special L source, supported by a passage-by-passage commentary on the whole Gospel.
books.note: Two volumes. Out of print; mostly available used.

books.title: Meeting Jesus Again for the First Time
books.subtitle: The Historical Jesus and the Heart of Contemporary Faith
books.author: Marcus J. Borg
books.summary: Contrasts the historical Jesus with the Jesus of traditional Christian belief and explores what that distinction means for faith today.

books.title: The Misunderstood Jew
books.subtitle: The Church and the Scandal of the Jewish Jesus
books.author: Amy-Jill Levine
books.summary: Argues that Christian readings of Jesus often distort the Judaism he lived in, and corrects common misconceptions about first-century Jewish life.

books.title: Narratives of a Vulnerable God
books.subtitle: Christ, Theology, and Scripture
books.author: William C. Placher
books.summary: A theological study of how the Gospel narratives portray Christ and what that implies for how Christians understand God.

books.title: The New Greek/English Interlinear New Testament
books.author: Robert K. Brown and Philip W. Comfort
books.summary: A Greek–English interlinear New Testament giving a word-for-word English translation beneath the UBS5/NA28 Greek text, with the New Revised Standard Version printed in a parallel column.
books.note: The episode's reading of Luke 10:25–37 uses Robert K. Brown's interlinear English from this volume.

books.title: The Origins of Totalitarianism
books.author: Hannah Arendt
books.summary: Traces how antisemitism, imperialism, and the decline of the nation-state prepared the ground for Nazi and Stalinist rule.

books.title: Parables and Presence
books.subtitle: Forms of the New Testament Tradition
books.author: Robert W. Funk
books.summary: A collection of essays on the literary forms of the New Testament tradition, chiefly the parables, including "The Good Samaritan as Metaphor," on how their language involves the hearer.

books.title: Poet & Peasant and Through Peasant Eyes
books.subtitle: A Literary-Cultural Approach to the Parables in Luke
books.author: Kenneth E. Bailey
books.summary: Combines literary analysis of the poetic structure of Luke's parables with study of Middle Eastern peasant culture to reconstruct how their first hearers would have understood them.
books.note: The episode cites Through Peasant Eyes (1980), now sold only in this combined edition.

books.title: The Power of Parable
books.subtitle: How Fiction by Jesus Became Fiction about Jesus
books.author: John Dominic Crossan
books.summary: Examines the parables as fiction told by Jesus and traces how the Gospel writers then turned them into fiction about him.

books.title: The Righteous Mind
books.subtitle: Why Good People Are Divided by Politics and Religion
books.author: Jonathan Haidt
books.summary: Argues that moral judgments come mainly from fast intuition, with reasoning mostly justifying them afterward, and uses moral psychology to explain why people divide over politics and religion.

books.title: The Samaritans
books.subtitle: A Profile
books.author: Reinhard Pummer
books.summary: A survey of the Samaritans from antiquity to the present, covering the literary, epigraphic and archaeological sources, their history, their Pentateuch, their rituals and customs, and the community today.

books.title: The Shock Doctrine
books.subtitle: The Rise of Disaster Capitalism
books.author: Naomi Klein
books.summary: Contends that free-market reforms have repeatedly been pushed through in the aftermath of wars, coups, and disasters, while the public is disoriented.

books.title: Short Stories by Jesus
books.subtitle: The Enigmatic Parables of a Controversial Rabbi
books.author: Amy-Jill Levine
books.summary: Levine, a Jewish New Testament scholar, reads the parables in their first-century Jewish setting rather than through later Christian allegory.

books.title: The Sneetches and Other Stories
books.author: Dr. Seuss
books.summary: A collection of four rhyming picture-book stories, including the title tale of star-bellied and plain-bellied creatures whose status distinctions are exploited and finally abandoned.

books.title: The System
books.subtitle: Who Rigged It, How We Fix It
books.author: Robert B. Reich
books.summary: Contends that concentrated corporate wealth has captured American politics and rewritten economic rules in its favor, and proposes reforms.

books.title: What's the Matter with Kansas?
books.subtitle: How Conservatives Won the Heart of America
books.author: Thomas Frank
books.summary: Examines why many working-class Kansans vote Republican against their economic interests, arguing that cultural grievance has displaced economic politics.

books.title: Why We're Polarized
books.author: Ezra Klein
books.summary: Argues that American political polarization stems from the sorting of party identities along racial, religious, and geographic lines, reinforced by media and political institutions.
